note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Parkway (Highway 93N), 60 km north of the Highway 1/93N junction in Banff National Park, in forest between Upper and Lower Waterfowl Lakes on the Mistaya River. One RV, one tent and one car a site; all vehicles must fit on the driveway. Saturday evening interpretive programs at the campground theatre. No cell coverage. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on Parks Canada's Banff pages: 110 unserviced first-come sites, C$26.75 a night plus Banff entry and fire permit, rigs to 9 m (31 ft), 2026 season June 18 - Sep 6 (stored 06-15..09-07 was note-derived), 14-night maximum, drinking water, flush and dry toilets, sani-dump. Wrote fees (entrance, 6 people, note), sites (max 30 -> 29), hookups, facilities (flush/vault/potable added), season, booking (manual, max stay 14); note rewritten.

The Banff contact page gives Lake Louise Visitor Centre 403-522-3833 (nearest staffed office), Banff Visitor Centre 403-762-1550, and campground reservations 1-877-RESERVE (1-877-737-3783). POLICY ROW federal:parks-canada: no contradiction found. This campground is first-come only (the row's own note says 'Many smaller campgrounds are first-come only'), so the entry's own reservable false moots the row's platform/url/reservation fee. The Banff entry fees (C$12.25 adult, C$24.50 family/group) and the C$17 Icefields fire permit match the row's note. The camping page also says 'Campground reservations may be made until 2 p.m. on date of booking' and 'Maximum stay – 14 nights' (park-wide rules; the row has no max_stay_nights - a possible row addition for Banff, not checked for other parks). reservation.pc.gc.ca answered 403 to plain HTTP (unread; not needed for a first-come campground).
MAX LENGTH: the page says 'up to 9 meters (31 feet)'; 9 m is 29.5 ft, so 29 written (stored 30 derived), following 8804's metre-first conversion. Either way above 23 ft.

FEE LABEL: the fees page calls the site type 'Unserviced with washroom building having toilets only', while the camping page lists flush toilets and 'Drinking water'; potable_water written from the camping page ('Potable water and greywater sinks are available'; other Icefields pages say RVs fill water here).
WEBSITE: the Banff camping page answered 200 (Google links its #waterfowl anchor). GOOGLE 4.9 from 68 reviews.

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront - confirmed): on Esri imagery (1 m/px) the loops sit in continuous spruce; the west loop road runs roughly 20-60 m from the Mistaya River's braided gravel channels with a belt of trees between, and the north end is about 100-150 m from Lower Waterfowl Lake through forest. Trees on the bank: not waterfront, and no view can be confirmed through the canopy.
PIN (51.84236,-116.62288): in the middle of the loops on imagery; Google's 51.84294,-116.62027 is ~190 m east near the entrance road. No move.
